english: The four observations $13,19,21,x$, where $x$ is an integer, have coefficient of variation $25\%$. When the same real number $c$ is added to each of these four observations, the coefficient of variation of the new observations becomes $40\%$. Then the value of $c$ is ______.
hindi: चार प्रेक्षणों $13,19,21,x$, जहाँ $x$ एक पूर्णांक है, का विचरण गुणांक $25\%$ है। जब इन चारों प्रेक्षणों में से प्रत्येक में एक ही वास्तविक संख्या $c$ जोड़ी जाती है, तब नए प्रेक्षणों का विचरण गुणांक $40\%$ हो जाता है। तब $c$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: CV $=\dfrac{\sigma}{\bar x}\times100=25$ means $\sigma=\dfrac{\bar x}{4}$, i.e. $16\sigma^2=\bar x^2$ (with $\bar x>0$).
Discriminant $=1802^2-4\cdot47\cdot14391=541696=736^2$, so $x=\dfrac{1802\pm736}{94}$, i.e. $x=27$ or $x=\dfrac{533}{47}$. As $x$ is an integer, $x=27$.
Check: $13,19,21,27$ have mean $20$, deviations $-7,-1,1,7$, variance $\dfrac{100}{4}=25$, $\sigma=5$, CV $=25\%$.
Adding $c$ to every observation leaves $\sigma=5$ and makes the mean $20+c$. CV $=40\%$: $\dfrac{5}{20+c}=\dfrac{2}{5}\Rightarrow20+c=12.5\Rightarrow c=-7.5$.
originality_note: New: an unknown observation is fixed by a CV condition (a quadratic with one integer root), and then a change of origin, which keeps sigma but moves the mean, is tuned to a new CV (way 3: object fixed by two conditions). Closest known: 'adding a constant changes CV'. Different because: sigma is not given; it comes from the quadratic for x, and the required shift is negative.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. The integer condition removes the second root 533/47. Changed: No change.
key_step: Setting up the CV condition as a quadratic in x and choosing the integer root, then using that a shift keeps sigma.
justification: Two ideas linked with a heavy quadratic and a root selection, in numerical format. Above 2026-P2-Q12 (L2); Level 3.

concept_use.Coefficient of variation and comparison: CV = sigma / mean x 100 gives 16 sigma^2 = mean^2, and the new CV 40 gives c.
